claims.explanation: GSK1070916 is a potent, long-residence Aurora B/C inhibitor that kills proliferating cells by disrupting mitosis and cytokinesis, so selectivity is driven by dependence on Aurora B/C activity and high proliferative/mitotic index rather than by a single lineage. Lines with high AURKB/AURKC expression, high mitotic gene programs, or loss of p53-mediated arrest/apoptosis should be most sensitive, whereas quiescent or Aurora-A-driven lines are relatively protected.

features.basis: direct drug target; Aurora B overexpression is common in tumors and predicts dependence
direct drug target with high potency (Ki 1.5 nM)
Aurora B substrate/partner; high mitotic program and survivin dependence; BIRC5 is strongly downregulated by drug in virtual cell
TPX2 activates Aurora A, which is poorly inhibited by GSK1070916; Aurora A-driven lines may escape
GSK1070916 is >250-fold selective over Aurora A, so Aurora A-dependent lines are less sensitive
loss of p53-mediated arrest/apoptosis after failed cytokinesis and polyploidy increases sensitivity
high mitotic/CDK1 activity indicates proliferating cells dependent on Aurora B; CDK1 is downregulated by drug
high proliferative/mitotic index; CCNA2 is downregulated by drug in virtual cell
PLK1 is a mitotic regulator and top transcriptional neighbor of GSK1070916; PLK1 inhibition is synergistic in T-ALL
MYC-driven proliferation increases mitotic dependence and Aurora B inhibitor sensitivity
loss of RB1 releases E2F and increases mitotic gene expression, enhancing dependence on Aurora B
CDKN2A loss increases proliferation and mitotic dependence
